page.heading: Ad Platform Integrations
page.description: Connect Google Ads and Meta Lead Ads to capture leads into your audiences. Each form/campaign maps to one audience — add multiple connectors for multiple audiences.

activeConnectors.title: Active Connectors
activeConnectors.description: Each row links one ad platform form to one audience.
activeConnectors.loadError: Could not load connectors. The integration API may not be deployed yet.

table.emptyDescription: Add a Meta or Google connector below to start receiving leads.
table.syncNow: Sync leads now (pull the last 24h from Meta)

editDialog.title: Edit default values
editDialog.description: Key/value pairs stamped onto every lead from this connector. Each key should match an audience custom field name (otherwise the value is just carried through as raw form data). Form payload values always take precedence over defaults.
editDialog.duplicateKeys: Duplicate keys detected — only the last value for each key will be kept.

fieldMapping.label: Field Mapping
fieldMapping.description: Map each platform field to an audience custom field. Unmapped fields are kept with original names.

google.audienceLabel: Main list (for campaigns you don't route)
google.howItWorks1: Choose the audience these leads should go to and create the connector.
google.howItWorks2: Paste the webhook URL and key we generate into your Google Ads lead form.
google.howItWorks3: Click "Send test data" in Google Ads. This page confirms when it arrives.
google.dialogDescription: Campaigns you haven't routed send their leads to {{audience}}.
google.dialogDescriptionNoAudience: Paste these two values into your Google Ads lead form.
google.setupStep1: In Google Ads, open the lead form you want to connect (under Assets) and edit it.
google.setupStep2: In the lead delivery section, choose "Webhook integration". Older accounts show it under "Export leads" → "Other data integration options".
google.setupStep3: Paste the Webhook URL and the Key above into their fields. Both must match exactly.
google.setupStep4: Click "Send test data". Google should report success, and the status below updates within a few seconds.
google.setupStep5: Save the lead form. Then route each campaign to its own list below; campaigns you don't route go to the main list.
google.statusWaiting: Nothing received from Google yet. Send test data from your Google Ads lead form; this updates automatically.
google.statusReceived: Google reached this connector on {{time}}. The setup works.
google.troubleshoot404: "Not found" (404): the webhook URL was copied incompletely, or this connector was deactivated. Copy the URL again.
google.troubleshoot401: "Unauthorized" (401): the Key in Google Ads does not match. Copy the key again; it is case-sensitive.
google.troubleshootNoLeads: Test data is never saved as a lead. Real leads appear once the form runs on a live campaign.

routes.heading: Campaigns → lead lists
routes.hint: Each Google campaign can send its leads to its own list, with that list's workflows and counsellors. Campaigns without a list send their leads to the main list, {{list}}.
routes.empty: No campaign has sent a lead yet. Campaigns appear here with their first lead, or add one below using its ID from Google Ads.
routes.newListHint: The new list gets the main list's form fields and notification emails. Set up its workflows and counsellors in Audience Manager.
routes.moveExisting: Also move this campaign's existing leads ({{count}}) to the new list
routes.addHeading: Route a campaign before its first lead (use its campaign ID from Google Ads)
routes.skipped: Leads not moved (already in that list): {{count}}
routes.saveError: Could not save the campaign routing
routes.autoListsLabel: Create a list automatically for each new campaign
routes.autoListsHint: On a campaign's first lead, it gets its own list with the main list's form fields, named after the campaign (name it here, even before its first lead) or "Google campaign" plus its ID until you do. A list of the same type and name is reused. Set up its workflows and counsellors in Audience Manager.
routes.autoListsOn: New campaigns will get their own list
routes.autoListsOff: New campaigns will go to the main list

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: Keys for the AI Evaluation API. A partner system (your ERP, OSM or test-series vendor) uses a key to create exams, send answer sheets and read AI marks for this institute.

disabled.title: Evaluation API is not enabled
disabled.description: Contact Vacademy to enable the Evaluation API

empty.title: No API keys yet
empty.description: Create a key and share it with the system that will call the Evaluation API.

scopes.evaluation_read: Read exams, submissions, results and credits
scopes.evaluation_write: Create exams, questions, rubrics, candidates, uploads and submissions
scopes.evaluation_review: Override AI marks and approve them

form.heading: Create API key
form.hint: Leave the expiry empty for a key that does not expire. The daily limit caps how many answer copies this key can send per day, within the institute's own limit.

errors.nameRequired: Enter a name for the key.
errors.nameTooLong: Keep the name to 120 characters or fewer.
errors.expiryInPast: The expiry date must be today or later.
errors.capInvalid: The daily limit must be a whole number above 0.
errors.generic: Check the form and try again.

issued.heading: Copy your API key
issued.warning: Store this key now. It is shown only once and cannot be shown again. If it is lost, revoke it and create a new one.
issued.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the key and copy it yourself.
issued.usage: Send it in the X-API-Key header to https://api.evalezy.com/v1.
issued.notCopiedWarning: You have not copied this key yet. Close again to discard it; it cannot be shown again.

revoke.title: Revoke this API key?
revoke.description: "{{name}}" stops working within a minute, and any system using it gets an error. This cannot be undone.

toasts.issueFailed: Could not create the API key.
toasts.revokeFailed: Could not revoke the API key.

loginLinks.title: Login links
loginLinks.description: Links that sign a learner in without a password, such as /go/<username>, /subscriptions/<username> and live-class links. Protect them with a code that expires.
loginLinks.requireLabel: Require a login code on every link
loginLinks.requireHint: Off (default): links work with just a username, as they always have, and any ?lc=<code> is ignored. On: a link must carry a valid ?lc=<code>, and username-only links stop working. Turn this on only after every system that sends learner links adds the code.
loginLinks.requireOnToast: Login links now need a code.
loginLinks.policyLoadError: Could not load this setting. Refresh to try again.
loginLinks.keysDescription: Your website or CRM server uses a key to get a login code for one learner, then adds ?lc=<code> to any learner-portal link. Keep keys on your server; never put one in a web page or app.
loginLinks.empty: No keys yet. You need one only if your own systems send learner links.
loginLinks.formHint: Leave the expiry empty for a key that does not expire.
loginLinks.issuedUsage: Your server sends the key in the X-API-Key header:
loginLinks.issuedThen: The response has a code. Add ?lc=<code> to the learner's link. Codes last up to 30 days.
loginLinks.confirmDescription: Every link that has only a username stops working for your learners straight away, including messages already sent. Check that every system that sends links adds a code first.

routes.title: Links that still work without a login code
routes.hint: Ticked links keep signing learners in from the username in the link, even while a login code is required. Every other link needs a valid code.
routes.warning: Anyone who knows a learner's username or email can sign in as them through a ticked link. Tick only the links you need.

catalogApi.title: Catalogue API & websites
catalogApi.description: Show your published courses on your own website and send its enquiries straight into your CRM.
catalogApi.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.

websites.title: Your websites
websites.description: Your keys only work on these websites (and on localhost while you build). Prove each website is yours by adding a DNS record.
websites.emptyDescription: Add the website that will show your courses, for example www.yourschool.com.

addDialog.heading: Add a website
addDialog.label: Website address
addDialog.hint: You can paste the full link. A verified website also covers its subdomains.

errors.host_invalid: This does not look like a website address.
errors.host_ip: Use your website's name, not an IP address.
errors.host_localhost: localhost always works, so there is no need to add it.
errors.host_single_label: Enter the full address, like yourschool.com.

dns.heading: Verify {{host}}
dns.intro: Add this TXT record where you manage your domain's DNS (GoDaddy, Cloudflare…). Then press Verify. DNS changes can take up to an hour.
dns.step1: Open the DNS settings of your domain, where you bought it or where it is hosted.
dns.step2: Create a new TXT record and copy in the name and value below.
dns.step3: Save it, come back here and press Verify now.
dns.name: Name
dns.nameHint: Some providers add your domain to the name for you. If yours does, enter only the part before your domain.
dns.verified: This website is verified. Your keys work on it now.
dns.noRecord: The DNS record is not available. Remove the website and add it again.

toasts.added: {{host}} added. Now add the DNS record.
toasts.notYet: No TXT record found yet. DNS changes can take up to an hour.
toasts.verifyFailed: Could not check the website right now. Try again in a minute.

removeConfirm.title: Remove {{host}}?
removeConfirm.description: Your keys will stop working on this website straight away. You can add it again later, but you will need to verify it again.

keys.empty: No keys yet. Create one when your website is ready to use the API.
keys.needsWebsite: Keys only work on verified websites. Add and verify your website above first.
keys.name: Name

errors.nameRequired: Enter a name for the key.

issued.heading: Your new key

issued.note: Safe to use in your website's code. It only reads your published catalogue and sends enquiries, and only works from your verified websites (and localhost).
